findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted
findings.body: The matchesSafely method returns false when the actual grant shortcut equals the expected shortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This inverts the intended check — it should return false (fail) when the shortcut does NOT match, but as written it fails precisely when it matches and otherwise falls through to return true even for wrong shortcuts. This means tests using isAccessTokenId effectively never properly validate the grant type shortcut and will reject the correct token IDs, causing false test failures or false negatives (letting incorrect token IDs pass undetected).

findings.title: Wrong variable null-checked for rawTokenId
findings.body: In the constructor, `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. As a result, a null `rawTokenId` will not be caught here, potentially leading to NPEs later when `rawTokenId` is used (e.g., string concatenation producing "null" instead of failing fast).

findings.title: Hardcoded refresh grant type note set unconditionally on token refresh/validation path
findings.body: In validateToken, `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN);` is set unconditionally whenever a token is being recreated/validated. This overwrites whatever grant type was originally used to create the client session context (e.g., authorization_code, device_code, ciba), even when this path is invoked for scenarios other than classic refresh-token grant (e.g. offline token refresh paths reused elsewhere), causing the encoded token ID's grant-type shortcut to incorrectly always read as 'rt' instead of the actual originating grant, undermining the stated purpose of the feature (correctly identifying grant type from the token ID).

findings.title: Non-atomic cache refresh for grant type shortcuts can race under concurrent token issuance
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut perform read-then-conditionally-write operations on ConcurrentHashMap without synchronization across the two maps (grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts). Although ConcurrentHashMap operations are individually thread-safe, the two maps can become inconsistent between each other under concurrent provider deployment/refresh scenarios, and the duplicate-shortcut validation done once in postInit is not re-run during runtime cache refresh, so a newly deployed grant type with a shortcut colliding with an existing one would silently overwrite entries without the earlier safety check that aborts startup.

findings.title: Access token ID format changed, breaking consumers that assume raw UUID token IDs
findings.body: Token IDs are now encoded with a 6-character context prefix followed by ':' and the raw UUID (e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...`). Any external or internal code/tests that previously assumed access token 'jti'/id is a plain UUID (e.g. length 36, UUID format validations, log parsing, DB lookups keyed by token id) will break. The PR already needed to update AssertEvents' isUUID-based matchers for this reason, indicating this is a breaking format change that should be clearly called out as such for downstream integrations relying on jti format.
